newsitem.title: UK: UK's Baldry "sorry" for mistakes on BSE.
newsitem.headline: UK's Baldry "sorry" for mistakes on BSE.

text.p: A British farm minister has apologised, albeit with a qualification, for any mistakes the government might have made in its handling of the crisis over the so-called mad cow disease BSE.
"If at any time we have erred I'm very sorry for that," UK junior farm minister Tony Baldry told the National Farmers Union's Annual General Meeting on Tuesday.
But he defended his Conservative party's role in supporting agriculture. Farm incomes had risen 65 per cent in real terms since the last election.
The government had committed 3.3 billion sterling to BSE related spending.
Liberal Democrat agriculture spokesman Paul Tyler criticised the government for not taking responsibility for failings in the handling of the BSE crisis.
Sorry was "just that magic word which would have transformed the situation," he said.
"It's 50 years since a minister of agriculture has resigned because he felt he'd let farmers down," Tyler said.
Tyler saw an increased emphasis on quality as a result of the BSE affair as a positive result.
Labour agriculture spokesman Gavin Strang rejected Baldry's accusation that Labour was urban biased. "I'm proud of British agriculture," he said.

Strang recognised the importance of the EU in the making of agriculture policy. As European policy changed, he meant to fight for a bigger share of agricultural production for the UK and identify environmental priorities, he said.
